nightdash-bot: NIGHTLY ALERT: eng-runtime nightly perf jump — short-seq 99p latency +18% vs baseline, throughput -9% in last hour. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/rt/shortseq :rotating_light:
alex: ugh saw the alert, pretty narrow to seq<=64. any suspect merges last night?
maya: last merge was #4582 (batch-prober: prefer small-batch stride) from dmitri. landed ~02:10 UTC.
carla: pinging @dmitri for context, that change reorders prober passes to prefer smaller strides, thought it would help coldstart.
dmitri: yep, intended to reduce cold miss penalty. didn't expect 99p blowup. will repro locally.
maya: repro steps I used:
```bash
perfbench run --workload=short --seq-max=64 --iter=300 --commit=origin/main
# measure p50/p95/p99 and kv cache hit-rate
```
maya: with commit abc1234 (pre-#4582) p99=68ms, with HEAD after #4582 p99=82ms. KV hit rate drops ~6% for short prefixes.
alex: interesting — smaller stride preferences could increase KV thrash if batching aligns differently. profiling?
maya: ran a short profiler, hottest traces:
```
kernel_selector::score() +14us
kv_cache::lookup_batch +9us
batch_coordinator::route_batches +6us
```
maya: score() calls increased and we see more frequent kernel handoffs (small kernel -> large kernel) causing extra memcpy.
dmitri: I pushed a lightweight change to scoreboard in #4582 that added an extra pass in prober ordering. probably introducing O(N) per-request overhead for tiny batches.
carla: CI nightly perf job also flagged a regression on the merge commit (job 3987). looks consistent with the dashboard.
eng-oncall: canary is at 20% for the rollout from last night, rollout window still open. recommend hold and revert if we can't mitigate quickly.
dmitri: opening a revert PR now -> https://github.com/redwood/ri/pull/4599 (revert: prefer-small-stride).
alex: before revert, can we try a quick tweak: disable the extra pass in prober via runtime flag and test in canary? config flag: `--prober-extra-pass=false`
maya: good idea. I pushed a canary override on canary hosts, re-running perfbench against canary pool.
maya: preliminary numbers with flag false: p99 drops back to ~70ms, kv hit-rate recovers ~4%. still slightly above baseline but much better.
dmitri: hmm ok that isolates it. revert PR open as fallback. I'll add a unit/benchmark test for small-batch path.
carla: please also add a trace-span around kernel_selector so we can instrument this path in nightdash next runs.
eng-oncall: holding rollout and paused automatic ramp. awaiting revert or config flip across all canary hosts.
alex: filing a short postmortem checklist: 1) revert PR if canary doesn't stabilize in 30m, 2) add microbenchmark for prober ordering, 3) add runtime opt and dashboard metric for prober-pass-count.
nightdash-bot: scheduled re-run of short-seq perfbench in 18 minutes, will post updated numbers.
maya: thanks — will keep logs attached to the PR. attaching local flame sample (snip): `kernel_selector::score` dominated during elevated p99.
dmitri: thx all. if revert lands I'll coordinate canary rollback and then re-land after benchmark + test.
nightdash-bot: UPDATE (18m): canary with `--prober-extra-pass=false` p99 improved to +3% vs baseline, overall throughput within 1%. monitoring for next 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
carla: leaving follow-up to add metric + perf-test. closing loop after stabilizes.
eng-oncall: good triage, keep an eye overnight. if anything spikes escalate to SRE.
nightdash-bot: THREAD CLOSED: will re-open if alert fires again.
